fact: On 2026-09-03 Kenya launched an official guide to investigating and prosecuting 76 listed cyber offences under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, presented by the Internal Security PS as the common operational framework under that Act.

The report says two false-publication sections of Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act were struck down by the Court of Appeal, and that a 2025 amendment to the Act was partly struck down in a later challenge, so the Act otherwise stands; published 2026-07-28, no event date given.

The report says Kenya's existing cybersecurity framework rests on the National Computer and Cybercrimes Coordination Committee under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, to which the new National Cybersecurity Agency (Legal Notice 89 of 2026) adds capacity; published 2026-09-11, no other date given.
The article says the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act has been put in place to address risks on digital platforms; no event date is given, so the published date 2026-09-08 is used.

The Nation reports the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act establishes a coordination committee and was amended by the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act, 2024, widening investigators' and courts' powers; no event date beyond the published date 2026-06-22 is used.
The Southern Africa Litigation Centre says Kenya's Court of Appeal struck down two sections of the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act in March 2026, leaving the rest of the Act in place.
